units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
Another pallor in the void, this time not violet, but a disagreeable smoky yellow.
With it, the whisper of a ghostly clarionet turning this tune into infinite sadness:
(Here there is another musical staff.)
The yellowish pallor moves: there is an old crone wandering in the void, bent and toothless; draped, as well as one can guess, in the coarse brown frock of some religious order.
She wanders and wanders in her slow hopeless way, much as a wasp flies in its rapid busy way, until she blunders against the thing she seeks: companionship.
With a sob of relief the poor old creature clutches at the presence of the man and addresses him in her dry unlovely voice, which can still express pride and resolution as well as suffering.
Excuse me; but I am so lonely; and this place is so awful.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: A new comer?
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Yes: I suppose I died this morning. I confessed; I had extreme unction; I was in bed with my family about me and my eyes fixed on the cross. Then it grew dark; and when the light came back it was this light by which I walk seeing nothing. I have wandered for hours in horrible loneliness.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: sighing.
Ah! you have not yet lost the sense of time. One soon does, in eternity.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Where are we?
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: In hell.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: THE OLD WOMAN [proudly] Hell!
I in hell!
How dare you?
unimpressed.
Why not, Senora?
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: You do not know to whom you are speaking. I am a lady, and a faithful daughter of the Church.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: I do not doubt it.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: But how then can I be in hell? Purgatory, perhaps: I have not been perfect: who has? But hell! oh, you are lying.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: Hell, Senora, I assure you; hell at its best--that is, its most solitary--though perhaps you would prefer company.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: But I have sincerely repented; I have confessed.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: How much?
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: More sins than I really committed. I loved confession.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: Ah, that is perhaps as bad as confessing too little. At all events, Senora, whether by oversight or intention, you are certainly damned, like myself; and there is nothing for it now but to make the best of it.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: THE OLD WOMAN [indignantly] Oh! and I might have been so much wickeder!
All my good deeds wasted!
It is unjust.
No: you were fully and clearly warned. For your bad deeds, vicarious atonement, mercy without justice. For your good deeds, justice without mercy. We have many good people here.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Were you a good man?
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: I was a murderer.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: A murderer! Oh, how dare they send me to herd with murderers! I was not as bad as that: I was a good woman. There is some mistake: where can I have it set right?
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: I do not know whether mistakes can be corrected here. Probably they will not admit a mistake even if they have made one.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: But whom can I ask?
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: I should ask the Devil, Senora: he understands the ways of this place, which is more than I ever could.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: The Devil! I speak to the Devil!
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: In hell, Senora, the Devil is the leader of the best society.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: I tell you, wretch, I know I am not in hell.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: How do you know?
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Because I feel no pain.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: Oh, then there is no mistake: you are intentionally damned.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Why do you say that?
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: Because hell, Senora, is a place for the wicked. The wicked are quite comfortable in it: it was made for them. You tell me you feel no pain. I conclude you are one of those for whom Hell exists.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Do you feel no pain?
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: I am not one of the wicked, Senora; therefore it bores me, bores me beyond description, beyond belief.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Not one of the wicked! You said you were a murderer.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: Only a duel. I ran my sword through an old man who was trying to run his through me.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: If you were a gentleman, that was not a murder.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: The old man called it murder, because he was, he said, defending his daughter's honor. By this he meant that because I foolishly fell in love with her and told her so, she screamed; and he tried to assassinate me after calling me insulting names.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: You were like all men. Libertines and murderers all, all, all!
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: And yet we meet here, dear lady.
units.name: DON JUAN
